text.p: SOLIDERE shares fell on Monday on the privately-operated Beirut Secondary Market (BSM) and dealers said a period of profit-taking might put-off the rise in prices during the coming days.
A shares fell to $114 from Friday's $115.625 on the BSM and B shares fell to $116 from $117.50. Both shares began rising 15 days ago.
"I think the period of profit-taking has begun. People who bought at lower prices are beginning to sell. This might slow the rise of the stocks during the coming few days," a dealer said.

Dealers said the rally was fuelled by expectations SOLIDERE will launch a $150 million GDR issue in October allowing non-Arab investors access to the market and the election victory of billionaire Prime Minsiter Rafik al-Hariri and allies which boosted confidence in the economy.
SOLIDERE has declined to comment on the report which followed rumours on the Beirut market.
Turnover on the BSM, which trades only SOLIDERE shares, fell to 7,551 shares against 11,668 on Friday and value was $878,948 from $1,362,200.5.
There was no trade on the official Beirut Stock Exchange (BSE) in any of the listed companies: Ciments Libanais, Ciments Blancs, Eternit and Uniceramic.
On Friday, only 2,500 Ciments Libanais shares were traded at $1.3125.
The LISPI index fell 0.38 percent to 84.80. The BLOM stock index fell 1.16 percent to 983.96. They cover both markets.
